mission_04: Relation Networks, introduced by Sung et al. (2018), extend metric-based meta-learning by learning the similarity function rather than using a fixed distance metric like Euclidean distance. The key innovation is a relation module — a neural network that takes the concatenation of a query embedding and a support prototype embedding and outputs a relation score between 0 and 1. This learned metric can capture more complex relationships than hand-crafted distances. The architecture has two components: (1) a feature embedding module that maps inputs to an embedding space, and (2) a relation module that computes similarity scores. Training is episodic: for each episode, compute relation scores between query examples and class prototypes, then optimize both modules using cross-entropy loss.
